title: Blake Anderson on the iOS app opportunity after Cal AI: build new, not copycats
summary: Starter Story visits the Cal AI founders in New York after the multi-million sale. Blake Anderson argues the App Store is still a huge, growing market, that copycats cap out at small outcomes, and that building something genuinely new has far more upside. The transcript has no speaker labels, so attribution is limited to the clearest statements.

principles.text: Even a $50M/year app is a tiny slice of the App Store, so the market is far bigger than any one hit.
principles.quote: People think Cali was this massive pie that we were eating from. We'll say Cali 50 mil per year. But then the app store as a whole, so the entire pie is 100 billion. We're 12,000th of the amount of total opportunity.

principles.text: The App Store market keeps growing, and applying new technology like AI expands the real opportunity.
principles.quote: It's a hundred billion today. It's growing over 10% year-over-year. I think almost within the next 6 years, it'll be over $200 billion spent just on the iOS app store alone.

principles.text: Copycat apps can reach $10K to $100K a month, but building something new has much higher potential.
principles.quote: It can work for getting to $10,000 a month or even $100,000 a month. But the reality is that I think you see much greater potential in outcomes when you are building something new.

principles.text: Original products attract better collaborators; a copycat pitch wouldn't have won him as a partner.
principles.quote: If Zach's initial DM to me had been like, "Hey, I created a copycat of this, I wouldn't have responded and we never would have worked together."
